title: Solve self-consistent mean-field equations
action: Implement a mean-field self-consistency solver for the uniaxial spin-1 Hamiltonian with given exchange (J0, ξ), single-ion anisotropy (D), and biquadratic exchange (K0, η, ζ) constants. Solve for the self-consistent values of σ = ⟨S̃^z⟩ and λ = ⟨Q̃^0⟩ across a dense grid of dimensionless temperature θ̃ = T/J0 and magnetic field h̃ = h/J0. Save the complete solution arrays for later use.
description: This intermediate step produces the σ and λ arrays required by all downstream scored computations. The evidence file documents that the self-consistency loop was executed, but it is not directly scored.

title: Compute order parameters for Figures 1 and 2
action: From the self-consistent σ and λ, evaluate the order parameter components ⟨S^z⟩, ⟨Q⁰⟩, and ⟨Q²⟩ using the relations derived from the mean-field Hamiltonian diagonalization. Generate temperature-dependent data for ⟨Q⁰⟩ at fixed dimensionless field h̃=4.5, and for ⟨Q²⟩ at h̃=4.7, 5.0, 5.3. Write a CSV file with columns for field, temperature, and the three order parameters.
description: CSV file containing the dimensionless field, temperature, and the three order parameter values for the conditions of Figures 1 and 2. The hidden checker will recompute the same quantities from the self-consistent equations and compare within tolerance.
output_schema: CSV with columns: field (float, dimensionless h/J0), temperature (float, dimensionless θ/J0), S_z (float), Q0 (float), Q2 (float). Rows must cover the curves shown in Fig.1 (h=4.5) and Fig.2 (h=4.7, 5.0, 5.3).

title: Determine QP1Z–ferromagnetic phase boundary
action: For a range of magnetic fields h̃, find the critical temperature θ̃_c at which ⟨Q²⟩ = 0 (within a small numerical tolerance). This defines the phase boundary between the QP1Z and ferromagnetic (FMP) phases. Output a CSV with (h̃, θ̃_c) pairs corresponding to Figure 3.
description: CSV file containing the dimensionless field and the critical temperature where ⟨Q²⟩ vanishes. The checker will verify each pair by recomputing ⟨Q²⟩ from the self-consistency equations at the given (h̃, θ̃_c) and checking it is ≤ tolerance.
output_schema: CSV with columns: field (float, dimensionless h/J0), critical_temperature (float, dimensionless θ_c/J0). Should cover the curve shown in Fig.3.

title: Critical temperature dependence on BEI anisotropy constants
action: Using the spin excitation spectrum stability condition ω₁(0)=0, compute the critical temperature θ̃* for the QP1Z→angular phase transition. For fixed fields h̃=2.5, 3.2, 3.8, evaluate θ̃* while varying η (with ζ=3.0) and varying ζ (with η=2.0) to reproduce Figure 4. Output a CSV with the anisotropy constants, field, and critical temperature.
description: CSV file containing the anisotropy constants, field, and critical temperature. The checker will recompute ω₁(0) from the agent's σ, λ and the given η, ζ, and verify that at the reported θ̃* the condition ω₁(0)=0 holds within tolerance.
output_schema: CSV with columns: eta (float, dimensionless), zeta (float, dimensionless), field (float, dimensionless h/J0), critical_temperature (float, dimensionless θ*/J0). Must include data for η=2.0 with varying ζ and ζ=3.0 with varying η, at fields 2.5, 3.2, 3.8.
